title.narrative: WGG- Building Inclusive Movements and Alliances in Kenya

description.narrative: It is a strategic platform for activists to participate in and learn about differing viewpoints, form creative alliances and highlight issues that are generally considered to be beyond the purview of women’s rights and gender justice.

sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

title.narrative: Number of Young Women and Women with Disabilities collectives with increased capacities to conduct international human rights advocacy towards developing inclusive and progressive global norms on Sexual and Gender Based Violence(SGBV) and political participation

description.narrative: Due to capacity-building programs and support through the consortium, young women and women with disabilities and their organisations can conduct international human rights advocacy towards developing inclusive and progressive global norms on SGBV and political participation.

title.narrative: No of occasions YW and WWDs participating in various advocacy platforms at local, national, regional spaces

description.narrative: As a result of WGG's work, Young women and women with disabilities are included in advocacy platforms: a place where they are often missed out\

comment.narrative: As the indicator measures any new values occurring since the start of the intervention,the baseline value is set at 0

1 - 15 GWWDs started attending Nyumba Kumi intitiative meetings in Kibera in Laini Saba and Lindi. They have been vocal in raising issues that pertain to women and girls with disbilities in their villages in regards to gender based violence. As a result more GWWDs have been specially invited to take part in the chief Barazas. The chief even invited GWWDs to have an office at the DCs office in Kibra.
Advocacy with the consortium during 16 days of campaign against GBV
16 day of campaign against gender based violence
Target has been set to zero, as the work described was taken up as an opportunity rather than planned.

6 girls and women were selected to be part of the Wangu Kanja GBV response Network, which is a network of rapid response GBV in Mukuru that support women and girls to seek aid, medical and legal after an assault.

There were significant transitions within the CREA East Africa (WGG) office, with both the Program Manager and Program Director transitioning out of the organization. These departures created a notable gap, which impacted the flow of work in the East Africa office, particularly as it took some time to fill both positions.

Women and Girls with Disabilities collectives engaged in two international and regional advocacy platforms that strengthened their capacity to participate in global human rights conversations on sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) and inclusive political participation. Through these engagements, representatives from the Kenya Women and Girls with Disabilities Network participated in global advocacy spaces where they contributed perspectives on the specific forms of SGBV affecting women and girls with disabilities and the structural barriers they face in political participation.

title.narrative: Number of Young Women and Women With Disability collectives with increased capacities to conduct human rights advocacy towards developing inclusive and progressive norms on SGBV at national and community levels

description.narrative: Due to capacity building programs, Young Women and Women With Disability collectives have increased capacities to conduct human rights advocacy

comment.narrative: As the indicator measures any new values occurring since the start of the intervention,the baseline value is set at 0

7 - 1) Partner trained 20 girls and women with disabilities from kibera to act as agents of change on gender based violence and inclusion of GWWDs in GBV dialogues in the community 2-7) Six WROs and DROs were strengthened through the Movement Strengthening Initiative which built cross-movement alliances by intentionally connecting movement actors across national borders and intersecting movements in East Africa. With this initial session we focused on bringing together the Feminist movement, the Disability Justice movement, the Sex worker movement, and the LBTQI+ movements. It was also intended to deepen awareness of issues related to Women with Disabilities (WWD) and young (trans-inclusive) women in the thematic area of Sexual and Gender-Based Violence. The MSI took place over a 6 month period of time and comprise four 3 hour long online sessions and a 3 day in-person workshop which took place in Nairobi.
Feminist Leadership and Movement Building Institute has been postponed to next year.5 collectives of women with disabilities and 5 collectives of young women had one training on the CEDAW mechanism

The target for this indicator was not achieved during the current reporting period because the timeframe for implementation was too short to adequately measure changes in the capacity of collectives of young women and women with disabilities to conduct sustained human rights advocacy on SGBV at national and community levels. Capacity strengthening and norm-influencing advocacy processes require longer engagement and continued monitoring before measurable results can be demonstrated.While several activities during the reporting period contributed to building awareness, connections, and exposure of young women and women with disabilities to advocacy platforms, the project period was not sufficient to determine whether these engagements translated into strengthened collective advocacy capacity at national and community levels. As a result, the indicator remains at 0 for this reporting cycle.Continued engagement and follow-up measurement would be required to assess whether the knowledge, networks, and opportunities created through the project lead to increased advocacy capacity among the collectives over time.

There were significant transitions within the CREA East Africa (WGG) office, with both the Program Manager and Program Director transitioning out of the organization. These departures created a notable gap, which impacted the flow of work in the East Africa office, particularly as it took some time to fill both positions.
